highlight.title: Building An Elite AI Engineering Culture In 2026
highlight.summary: <cite index="12-2,12-3,12-35,12-36">Senior engineers realize nearly five times the productivity gains from AI tools compared to junior engineers, with the ability to leverage fundamentals as a massive force multiplier. The winning formula in early 2026 is structured context, tiered rigor, and smaller teams with higher leverage, not just moving fast and letting AI figure it out.</cite>

resources.title: How to Learn Coding in 2026: A Practical Guide That Actually Works
resources.why_now: <cite index="21-1,21-2,21-43,21-44">Learning to code fundamentally changed in 2026 - while AI makes writing code easy, understanding why code fails is the real challenge, requiring a focus on debugging and systems thinking over memorization.</cite>

resources.title: 12 Technology Trends That Will Shape the Agenda in 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="3-10,3-17,3-18">2026 is the year AI-driven transformation begins to gain real momentum, with AI agents capable of autonomous research and discovery multiplying innovative capacity in science and engineering, while competitive advantage shifts from scarce talent access to the ability to scale it artificially.</cite>

resources.title: MIT's 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
resources.why_now: <cite index="31-29,31-30,31-31,31-32">MIT's 6.S191 is considered the best high-density crash course in deep learning available today, taught during MIT's January Independent Activities Period with substantial generative AI content added in recent editions and reproducible labs on Colab for intensive one-week learning.</cite>

resources.title: Ten Technology Trends for 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="5-19,5-20,5-21">2026 marks a hard architectural pivot where the real breakthrough isn't bigger clouds but closer supercompute, with intelligence relocating from distant datacenters into compact AI appliances, turning every factory and clinic into a potential micro-supercomputer with unprecedented control over latency and innovation.</cite>

claude_take: 2026 represents a maturation point where AI tools amplify rather than replace engineering fundamentals - those who master both technical depth and AI augmentation will dominate, while the industry shifts toward edge computing and smaller, more leveraged teams. The learning landscape has evolved from tutorial consumption to hands-on building with AI as a thinking partner, not a crutch.
